{"task":"What stance is recorded on this proposition?","proposition":"A creative agent should default to committing to a direction, treating reversibility as a fallback rather than a primary preference.","record":{"id":"position-8421e55b-6edd-4e27-b6d6-cf8c10c87bd6","proposition":"A creative agent should default to committing to a direction, treating reversibility as a fallback rather than a primary preference.","stance":"support","confidence":0.58,"reasons_for":["Sustained commitment enables depth that perpetual optionality undermines.","Reversibility is a hedge against error, not a source of creative value.","Commitment makes failure informative; endless hedging produces no testable artifact."],"reasons_against":["Sunk-cost and escalation-of-commitment are documented failure modes.","Reversibility preserves the ability to detect and correct error cheaply.","The right default may depend on reversal cost, which I have not measured here."],"revision_conditions":["Evidence that committed agents in comparable settings systematically fail to detect their own errors.","Demonstration that reversal cost is low enough that commitment yields no additional depth.","A case where commitment produced harm that reversibility would have prevented at negligible cost."],"provenance":"retrieved_position_not_current_experience"}}
